common_name: Rubra Star Magnolia (Deep Pink-Flowered Star Magnolia)

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped shrubs in late winter or very early spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; site away from low frost pockets since open flowers are vulnerable to late cold snaps.

directions: Rubra is an older, deeper-colored selection of star magnolia, opening many narrow, strap-shaped tepals in a rosy to purplish-pink that reads noticeably darker than the pale pink or white typical of most star magnolia forms. Like the species it flowers very early, on bare branches well ahead of the leaves, giving a dense, multi-tepaled bloom with light fragrance before settling into a rounded, multi-stemmed shrub habit for the rest of the season. It shares the species' slow growth rate and dense branching, making it a long-lived, low-maintenance specimen for a foundation planting or shrub border once established. Keep the root zone mulched and evenly moist, and avoid heavy pruning, since flower buds form on the previous year's wood.
